key_insight: Compact multimodal language models can support structured pulmonary embolism question answering, especially when combining CTPA with EHR evidence.
clinical_relevance: The study suggests these models may help early PE risk detection and explanation across both diagnostic and prognostic clinical tasks.
method: Built INSPECT-based benchmark with 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients.
Reframed 8 PE diagnostic/prognostic tasks as structured clinical question answering.
Compared efficient MLLMs under CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR settings with zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
evidence_signal: Across evaluations, Gemma4 E4B and Gemma4 E2B performed best when EHR was available, and PE diagnosis was easier than prognostic prediction, especially readmission.
watch_item: Performance was lower for prognostic tasks and readmission prediction, so these models should be treated as decision-support tools rather than standalone risk predictors.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
